column2: The city decided to scrap the old buses and buy electric ones.
column3: 市政府決定報廢老舊公車，改買電動車。
column4: scrap an old car (報廢舊車)
column5: scrap 本來是碎片，舊東西拆成碎片就是報廢

column2: She scraped the burnt rice off the bottom of the pot.
column3: 她把黏在鍋底的燒焦飯刮了下來。
column5: scrape 唸起來像刀子刮東西的「斯可瑞」聲

column2: She scrolled down the page to find the price of the shoes.
column3: 她把頁面往下捲動，找那雙鞋的價格。
column4: scroll down the page (向下捲動頁面)
column5: scroll 原指捲軸，手指一滑就像攤開捲軸往下看

column2: The teacher segmented the long text into four short parts for the class.
column3: 老師把長文章切成四個短段落給全班讀。
column5: seg 和 section 一樣有切開的味道，像把橘子切成一瓣瓣

column2: He sharpened his pencil before the math test began.
column3: 數學考試開始前，他先把鉛筆削尖。
column5: sharp 尖的 + en 使變 → 使變尖

column2: The baseball shattered the window into a hundred tiny pieces.
column3: 那顆棒球把窗戶砸成了上百片小碎片。
column5: 「瞎特」一聲，玻璃就碎了一地

column2: Tall trees shield the small garden from the strong wind.
column3: 高大的樹木替小花園擋住強風。
column4: shield from the sun (遮擋陽光)
column5: shield 是盾牌，當動詞就是拿盾擋在前面保護

column2: The children shivered at the bus stop on the freezing morning.
column3: 在寒冷的早晨，孩子們在公車站牌旁冷得發抖。
column5: 冷到縮成一團，嘴裡發出「嘶、窩」的聲音

column2: He shoved his way through the crowd to catch the last train.
column3: 他推開人群擠過去，想趕上末班車。
column5: shove 唸「聳夫」，聳起肩膀硬推過去

column2: Please shred these old bank statements before you throw them away.
column3: 丟掉這些舊的銀行對帳單之前，請先用碎紙機銷毀。
column4: shred confidential documents (銷毀機密文件)
column5: shred 的碎紙機把紙變成一條條細絲

column2: The little girl shrieked with joy when she saw the puppy.
column3: 小女孩看到小狗時高興得尖叫起來。
column5: shriek 唸「許瑞克」，開心或受驚時發出「咿——」的尖叫

column2: She shuddered at the thought of walking alone through the dark forest.
column3: 一想到要獨自走過漆黑的森林，她就忍不住發抖。
column4: shudder at the thought (一想到就發抖)
column5: shudder 像「瞎抖的」，想到可怕的畫面就瞎抖

column2: The owner shuttered his shop early because a typhoon was coming.
column3: 因為颱風要來了，老闆提早把店關了。
column5: shut 關上 + ter；百葉窗一拉下來，店就收了

column2: Let the soup simmer over low heat for twenty minutes.
column3: 讓湯用小火燉煮二十分鐘。
column4: simmer over low heat (小火慢燉)
column5: 湯在鍋裡小聲滋滋冒泡但沒大滾，就是 simmer

column2: He slammed the door so hard that the pictures on the wall shook.
column3: 他用力甩上門，震得牆上的畫都晃動了。
column5: slam 的聲音就像「砰」，甩門就是 slam the door

column2: In the old movie, she slapped him across the face and walked away.
column3: 在那部老電影裡，她打了他一巴掌，轉身走開。
column5: slap 和拍手的「啪」聲很像，一巴掌就是 slap

column2: According to the legend, the brave prince set out to slay the dragon.
column3: 根據傳說，勇敢的王子出發去屠龍。
column5: slay 和 play 押韻，童話裡的英雄用 slay 打倒大龍

column2: Car sales slumped sharply after the price of gasoline went up.
column3: 汽油價格上漲後，汽車銷量大幅下滑。
column5: slump 像洩氣的皮球「噗」一聲癱下去

column2: A huge wave smashed the little boat against the rocks.
column3: 一個巨浪把小船砸向岩石，撞得粉碎。
column5: smash 是 mash 搗爛前面加 s，用力一砸就碎成泥

column2: The dog snarled at the stranger and showed its sharp teeth.
column3: 那隻狗對陌生人低吼，露出尖尖的牙齒。
column5: snarl 唸「斯拿」，狗低聲「嗚嗚」地吼

column2: A seagull snatched the sandwich right out of her hand.
column3: 一隻海鷗從她手中直接把三明治搶走。
column5: snatch 唸「斯內奇」，手一伸快速抓走

column2: The boy sneaked out of the classroom while the teacher was writing.
column3: 老師寫字的時候，男孩偷偷溜出了教室。
column4: sneak into a room (溜進房間)
column5: sneakers 運動鞋走起路來沒聲音，sneak 就是悄悄走

column2: The puppy sniffed the grass to find where the ball had landed.
column3: 小狗在草地上嗅來嗅去，找球掉到哪裡。
column5: sniff 就是吸鼻子的聲音「斯尼夫」

column2: My grandfather snores so loudly that I can hear him through the wall.
column3: 我爺爺打呼聲大到隔著牆我都聽得到。
column5: snore 唸「斯挪」，睡覺時鼻子發出「挪——挪——」

column2: When he heard the excuse, Dad snorted and shook his head.
column3: 聽到那個藉口，爸爸輕蔑地哼了一聲，搖了搖頭。
column4: snort with contempt (輕蔑地哼一聲)
column5: snort 是鼻子噴氣，豬和馬都會 snort

column2: Soak the beans in water overnight so they cook faster.
column3: 把豆子泡在水裡一整夜，煮起來會比較快。
column5: 豆子泡進水裡吸飽水，so-ak 像慢慢吸收

column2: A little butter will soften the hard cheese.
column3: 加一點奶油會讓硬起司變軟。
column4: soften the tone (使語氣變柔和)
column5: soft 柔軟 + en 使變 → 使變軟

column2: The young pilot soloed for the first time after ten hours of training.
column3: 這位年輕的飛行員受訓十小時後，第一次單飛。
column4: solo for the first time (第一次單飛)
column5: solo 像「梭囉」，一個人梭出去獨自行動

column2: The teacher's praise spurred him to practice even harder.
column3: 老師的稱讚激勵他更加努力練習。
column5: spur 是馬刺，一刺馬就跑得更快，人被刺激就更有衝勁

column2: He stacked the clean dishes carefully next to the sink.
column3: 他把洗乾淨的盤子小心地疊在水槽旁。
column5: stack 像 stuck，東西一層層堆起來卡在一起

column2: After running the marathon, she staggered across the finish line.
column3: 跑完馬拉松後，她搖搖晃晃地跨過終點線。
column4: stagger to one's feet (搖搖晃晃站起來)
column5: 想像剛出生的小鹿腿軟，歪歪倒倒地走路

column2: Red wine stained the white tablecloth during the party.
column3: 派對中，紅酒把白色桌巾染髒了。
column5: 污漬洗不掉，心裡真「斯疼」

column2: The mayor staked his reputation on finishing the bridge by June.
column3: 市長賭上自己的名聲，保證六月前完成這座橋。
column5: stake 和 steak 同音，想像押上一塊牛排當賭注

column2: The old car stalled in the middle of the busy intersection.
column3: 那輛舊車在繁忙的十字路口中央拋錨了。
column5: stall 原指馬廄的隔間，車子像被關住動不了

column2: The sudden thunder startled the baby, and she began to cry.
column3: 突然的雷聲嚇到了寶寶，她哭了起來。
column5: start 開始 + le；突然「start」一下，被嚇一跳

column2: She steered the boat carefully around the rocks.
column3: 她小心地掌舵，讓船繞過那些岩石。
column5: steer 唸「斯提」，手握方向盤把方向「提」正

column2: Teachers should not stereotype students by the schools they come from.
column3: 老師不該根據學生來自哪所學校就給他們貼標籤。
column4: stereotype a group (對某群體貼刻板標籤)
column5: stereo 固定 + type 印版 → 每個人都印成同一個模子

column2: The old gym bag began to stink after a week in the hot car.
column3: 那個舊運動袋在熱車裡放了一週後開始發臭。
column4: stink of fish (散發魚腥臭味)
column5: stink 和 think 押韻，臭到沒辦法思考

column2: He stooped to pick up the coin lying under the bench.
column3: 他彎下腰撿起長椅下的硬幣。
column4: stoop to pick up (彎腰撿起)
column5: 彎腰時背會凸起來，stoop 唸「斯凸」

column2: Please straighten the picture on the wall; it is hanging crooked.
column3: 請把牆上的畫掛正，它歪掉了。
column5: straight 直的 + en 使變 → 使變直
